title: Explicit simplicial bar projective resolution of a cofibrant-valued diagram
statement:
Use the model and simplicial-model terminology of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], and the projective diagram model structures of [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial simplicial model category, meaning that its underlying category is locally presentable and its two model weak factorization systems are generated by small sets. Here locally presentable means generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some regular $\kappa$ by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve these colimits. Fix universes in which the ordinary category $I$ is small and let $V:I\to\mathcal M$ have cofibrant values. Use the simplex category and simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Write $X\otimes K$ for the simplicial tensor. For $p\geq0$ define an $I$-diagram
$$S_pV(j)=\coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_p\to j}V(i_0).$$
Its action on $j$ postcomposes the final arrow. In the simplicial $p$ direction, $d_0$ applies $V(i_0\to i_1)$ to the value, internal faces compose adjacent arrows, the last face composes $i_{p-1}\to i_p\to j$, and degeneracies insert identities among $i_0,\ldots,i_p$. Define
$$QV(j)=\int^{[p]\in\Delta} S_pV(j)\otimes\Delta^p.$$
The coend is the coequalizer of the two maps from the coproduct over simplex operators to the coproduct over simplex objects, imposing the tensor/simplicial-operator relations; $\Delta^p=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(-,[p])$. Composition along the chain defines a natural augmentation $QV\to V$. The $I$-diagram $QV$ is projectively cofibrant and this augmentation is an objectwise weak equivalence. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{colim}_{I}QV\cong R_I(V):=\int^{[p]\in\Delta}\left(\coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_p}V(i_0)\right)\otimes\Delta^p.$$
Under this isomorphism every cocone $V\to\operatorname{const}A$ induces the same map to $A$ on both sides, by its component at $i_0$ followed by the tensor collapse $\Delta^p\to\Delta^0$. All constructions are functorial in maps of $I$-diagrams. The assertion includes the empty category $I$.

source.place: Dugger, A Primer on Homotopy Colimits, Section 9.2, Proposition 9.11, Corollary 9.8 and Remark 9.12 (the forward-chain version Q prime), printed pp.34-38; Section 19.1 and Theorem 19.4, printed pp.90-91, extend the construction to simplicial model categories. No Stacks tag states this simplicial model-category theorem. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: For a morphism $j\to k$, send the summand with final arrow $i_p\to j$ to the summand with its composite $i_p\to k$, acting identically on $V(i_0)$. The face formulas in the statement compose arrows, except that $d_0$ applies the first arrow through $V$; degeneracies insert identity arrows. Two faces in either order give the same composite by associativity and functoriality, two degeneracies insert the same identities, and a face next to an inserted identity cancels it; these are the simplicial identities. Composing the whole chain gives $V(i_0)\to V(j)$, and the identities just checked make these maps an augmented simplicial diagram. Tensor collapse to $\Delta^0$ therefore descends through the coend relations to $QV\to V$. All indexing sets are small since $I$ and $\Delta$ are small, and all coproducts and coequalizers exist by cocompleteness.

source.place: Section 9.2, Proposition 9.11 and Remark 9.12 (forward-chain Q prime); Section 19.1 for simplicial tensors, printed pp.37-38 and 90.

proof.text: Put $F_i(A)(j)=\coprod_{I(i,j)}A$. A natural map $F_i(A)\to Z$ is uniquely determined by the map $A\to Z(i)$ on $1_i$, because its component on $u:i\to j$ must be $Z(u)$ after that map. Thus $S_nV=\coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_n}F_{i_n}(V(i_0))$. Call such a chain nondegenerate when none of its $n$ internal arrows is an identity; no condition is imposed on the separate arrow $i_n\to j$. Removing identity arrows has a unique result, and the positions removed specify a unique surjection $[n]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$. Consequently the simplicial latching object $L_nS$ is the coproduct of precisely the degenerate summands: all multiple degeneracy presentations of one summand are identified by their common presentation with all identities removed. At each $j$, $L_nS(j)\to S_nV(j)$ is therefore inclusion of a subcoproduct with cofibrant complementary summands. It is a cofibration: a lifting problem against a trivial fibration extends over each complementary $V(i_0)$ by its cofibrancy. By the cited Reedy criterion $S_\bullet V(j)$ is Reedy cofibrant. These statements include $n=0$, when the latching object is initial.

source.place: Proposition 9.11 and Remark 9.12, printed pp.37-38; explicit latching calculation for their bar construction.

proof.text:
Let $Q^{(n)}$ be the coend coequalizer restricted to objects $[p]$ with $0\leq p\leq n$ and simplex operators between these objects, taken objectwise as an $I$-diagram; set $Q^{(-1)}$ to be the initial diagram. The inclusions of these truncated indexing categories give the skeletal filtration. The coend relations and the unique identity-removal factorization in Step 2 show that $Q^{(n-1)}\to Q^{(n)}$ is the pushout of the coproduct, over nondegenerate chains $i_0\to\cdots\to i_n$, of
$$F_{i_n}(V(i_0)\otimes\partial\Delta^n)\longrightarrow F_{i_n}(V(i_0)\otimes\Delta^n).$$
The boundary is attached by the $n+1$ faces. Their overlaps agree by the simplicial identities of Step 1; degenerate chains already factor through earlier stages, so add no cells. To verify this pushout without a skeletal-filtration theorem, a map from the proposed stage to a diagram $T$ is exactly a map from the previous stage together with one map $F_{i_n}(V(i_0)\otimes\Delta^n)\to T$ for each nondegenerate chain, agreeing on its boundary with the prescribed face maps. A degenerate chain contributes no free choice: its map is forced by its unique shorter chain and the associated surjection of simplices. The simplicial identities give agreement on boundary overlaps and between different strings of elementary degeneracies. Conversely these agreements impose all the coend relations, since every monotone operator factors as a surjection followed by an injection, and each factor is a composite of elementary degeneracies or faces. This proves the pushout universal property in both directions and gives the coend itself as $\operatorname{colim}_{n\geq0}Q^{(n)}$. Tensoring by a fixed simplicial set preserves the coproducts used here: the tensor-cotensor adjunction identifies maps out of such a tensor with maps out of the original coproduct into the corresponding cotensor, hence with families of maps from its summands. To prove each attaching map is a projective cofibration, let $E\to B$ be any projective trivial fibration, hence objectwise a trivial fibration by [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. By the explicit free-diagram adjunction of Step 2 a cell lifting problem is a lifting problem for $V(i_0)\otimes\partial\Delta^n\to V(i_0)\otimes\Delta^n$ against $E(i_n)\to B(i_n)$. The same tensor-cotensor adjunction gives $0\otimes K=0$ for every simplicial set $K$, hence $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(0,Z)$ is the terminal simplicial set. Thus the corner map of the simplicial mapping axiom applied to $0\to V(i_0)$ is exactly the map below. The axiom gives a trivial Kan fibration $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(V(i_0),E(i_n))\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(V(i_0),B(i_n))$. By the boundary-lifting characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] this lifts against $\partial\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$, including $n=0$. Tensor adjunction gives the required cell lift. Choose these lifts at each stage and take their compatible colimit; this proves $0\to QV$ lifts against every projective trivial fibration, hence is a projective cofibration. No hypothesis on the arrows of $V$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 9.11, Remark 9.12 and Section 19.1, printed pp.37-38 and 90: projective lifting proof, expanded here as the nondegenerate-chain cell filtration.

proof.text: Fix $j\in I$. Let $t_{-1}:V(j)\to S_0V(j)$ include the summand $j\xrightarrow{1_j}j$. For $n\geq0$ let $t_n$ send the summand $i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j$ identically on its $V(i_0)$-label to the summand $i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j\xrightarrow{1_j}j$. The last face composes the two last arrows, giving $d_{n+1}t_n=1$. In degree zero the other face applies $V(i_0\to j)$ and lands in the identity summand, so $d_0t_0=t_{-1}\varepsilon$. For $n\geq1$, any earlier face acts on the old part of the chain (including applying $V$ for $d_0$), giving $d_it_n=t_{n-1}d_i$ for $0\leq i\leq n$. Inserting an old identity commutes with appending the last arrow, giving $s_it_n=t_{n+1}s_i$ for $0\leq i\leq n$; finally $\varepsilon t_{-1}=1$. Step 2 supplies exactly the Reedy cofibrancy required by [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-extra-degeneracy]. That theorem gives $QV(j)\to V(j)$ a weak equivalence. Doing this for every $j$ proves the augmentation is an objectwise weak equivalence; the contraction need not be natural in $j$.

source.place: Definition 3.11 and Proposition 3.12, printed pp.12-13 (sinklike contraction); Remark 9.12, printed p.38, and Section 19.1, printed p.90.

proof.text: For fixed $i$ and $A$, a cocone $F_i(A)\to\operatorname{const}T$ is uniquely a map $A\to T$: the arrow $u:i\to j$ carries the $1_i$ summand to the $u$ summand, so the cocone equation forces the same map on every summand. Hence $\operatorname{colim}_IF_i(A)\cong A$, with this explicit universal cocone. More directly, a cocone $QV\to\operatorname{const}T$ is a family of maps $V(i_0)\otimes\Delta^n\to T$ indexed by chains $i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j$, subject to the simplex-operator and terminal-arrow relations. The terminal-arrow relation identifies the map for $u:i_n\to j$ with the map for $1_{i_n}$, and imposes no further relation: define the map for any $u$ by that for $1_{i_n}$ to obtain the inverse correspondence. The remaining relations are exactly the coend relations defining $R_I(V)$. Thus cocones out of $QV$ and maps out of $R_I(V)$ correspond, naturally in $T$, giving the displayed isomorphism. For a cocone $c_i:V(i)\to A$, the map on a chain is tensor collapse followed by $c_{i_0}$; it also equals composition along the chain followed by $c_j$, since $c_jV(i_0\to j)=c_{i_0}$. This verifies both coend relations and the asserted compatibility with the augmentation-induced cocone.

source.place: Corollary 9.8 and Remark 9.12, printed pp.36-38; the universal-property calculation is written out rather than using interchange of colimits as a black box.

proof.text: A natural transformation $V\to W$ acts on every chain summand by $V(i_0)\to W(i_0)$. Its naturality square for the first arrow verifies compatibility with $d_0$; all other operators merely change the indexing chain. Hence it induces the maps of coends and augmentations, and the formula in Step 5 makes the colimit isomorphism natural. If $I$ is empty, its diagram category is the terminal category, so its unique diagram is cofibrant and its augmentation is an objectwise weak equivalence vacuously. There are no chains, so all displayed coproducts and the coend $R_I(V)$ are initial; this is the colimit of the empty diagram. This proves every clause also in the empty case.

source.place: Remark 9.12, printed p.38: functorial bar construction; empty-index case checked directly.

proof_origin.place: Dugger, A Primer on Homotopy Colimits: Definition 3.11 and Proposition 3.12, pp.12-13; Corollary 9.8, Proposition 9.11 and Remark 9.12, pp.36-38; Section 19.1 and Theorem 19.4, pp.90-91.
